title: QA round: transcript export & blog publishing pipeline
description:
# Manual QA review — transcript export & blog publishing pipeline

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; tell me to commit or delete it when we are done.
(The previous, closed round is archived next to it in
`QA_REVIEW-permissions-round.md`.)

**Build under test:** `4e4a58b` (session transcript export) and `674939b` (blog
publishing pipeline). `ec19281` is beads bookkeeping, nothing to test.
**Re-run Setup after any fix.**

Origin: two features shipped together with heavy unit coverage but zero contact
with a real agent's payloads or a real published page. Everything below is what
the suite structurally cannot reach.

## Status

| #   | Case                                                                           | State                                                           |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | Live export of a real claude turn                                              | **PASS** — evidence-checked below                               |
| 2   | `:LouiselmToMarkdown` input paths (cancel, blank, `~`, bad dir, bad id)        | **DONE** — 2.1-2.3, 2.5 pass; 2.4 still open (`louiselm-euj`, reconfirmed, deferred) |
| 3   | Export mid-stream and while a permission decision is open                      | **PASS** — 3a and 3b both confirmed                             |
| 4   | Resumed-session export vs the live export of the same session                  | **found a gap** — `louiselm-d2o`, see F3 (out-of-repo)          |
| 5   | `create-blog.sh` against a real session id                                     | **PASS**, reproduces F3 as predicted                            |
| 6   | `render-post.sh` + `myst build` — does the highlighted fragment reach the page | **confirmed broken** — `louiselm-xrf`, see F4                   |
| 7   | GitLab CI pipeline                                                             | **not runnable locally** — `louiselm-8na` tracks the known risk |

## What the test suite already covers — skip these

Do not spend a round on them:

- Transcript merge/render logic against synthetic events (`tests/session/transcript_spec.lua`, 12 cases:
  chunk merging, interleaved tool calls, missing status/title fallbacks, determinism).
- Headless export against the mock agent, including timeout, agent crash during
  `session/load`, invalid config, stdout/stderr/exit-code contract
  (`tests/session/transcript_export_spec.lua`).
- `Chat:to_markdown` default path, explicit session id, disposed UI, not-attached id
  (`tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua`).
- Command registration and the `vim.ui.input` flow _with a stubbed input_
  (`tests/ui/command_spec.lua`).
- CSS namespacing against **real** `:TOhtml` output, and render-post idempotency
  (`blog/scripts/test-render-post.sh`); scaffold + mock-agent export (`test-create-blog.sh`).

## Setup

The plugin is installed as a clone of this repo, so new commits are not live
until you update it:

```vim
:lua vim.pack.update({ 'louiselm.nvim' })
```

Confirm in the buffer it opens (`:write`), restart nvim, then:

```bash
# these two must print the same commit
git -C ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim log --oneline -1
git -C ~/code/louiselm log --oneline -1
node -v            # cases 5-6 need Node 20+; CI pins node:24
```

For case 6 only, matching what CI pins:

```bash
npm install -g mystmd@1.10.1   # or use npx mystmd@1.10.1 in place of `myst`
```

**Permission mode matters for case 3b.** Some sessions in this round were
deliberately launched with the underlying agent's approval gate skipped
(`--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions`), by design, to see what happens under
reduced control. That's a legitimate thing to test, but it means the ACP
`session/request_permission` call never fires, so `louiselm`'s diff-review UI
never opens — not because of a remembered rule, a bug, or anything in this
repo, but because the agent process itself never asks. **Case 3b needs a
session launched *without* that flag** — confirm before running it, since
nothing in the UI signals which mode a session is in.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

Carried over from the permissions round and still true:

- **Pin the log by session id**, never `ls -t | head -1` — the newest log is the
  session you are talking to me in:
  `L=$(grep -l "<acp-session-uuid>" ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/*jsonrpc.log | tail -1)`.
  Get the id from the chat header or `:LouiselmSessionId`.
- **The log only holds the agent's side.** Your own prompts are not in it — which
  is exactly why `record_user` exists, and why case 1 checks the prompt text
  against what you typed, not against the log.
- **Say the tool name and give absolute paths** in prompts, or the model picks a
  different tool and the case misses.

New for this round:

- **`## ` inside agent text is indistinguishable from a section header.** The
  export writes `## User` / `## Assistant` / `## Tool:` with no escaping, and
  agents write markdown headings all the time. Any script that parses the export
  by section will over-count. Grep for `toolCallId = "..."` instead — that is the
  reliable anchor, and it is what the evidence check below uses.
- **The jsonrpc log is cumulative for the whole live conversation, not scoped to
  one turn.** Case 1's evidence check was run against the log *after* several
  more turns had already happened in the same ACP session (this QA round itself
  ran inside the session under test — the assistant answering your reports and
  the agent that produced the case-1 export are the same session). Diffing the
  export straight against the full log falsely showed 37 "missing" tool calls
  and out-of-order ids — they were all from later turns that postdated the
  export. Fix: take the log's tool-call id list, restrict it to the prefix
  ending at the last id that also appears in the export, and diff *that* prefix.
  Anything after is expected, not a bug — but say so explicitly rather than
  silently truncating.
- **Prompts as fenced code, not blockquotes.** A `> quoted` prompt often copies
  with the leading `>` attached from a rendered markdown pane, forcing an edit
  before pasting into nvim's input line. Fenced code blocks paste clean. Cases
  below now use fences for exactly this reason.
- **Flag order/state dependencies between sub-cases explicitly.** Case 2's five
  sub-points run against the same open chat/session state, back to back. If an
  earlier one leaves the UI in a bad state (stuck `decision_active`, focus in
  the wrong window, an uncaught error), a later sub-point can fail for a reason
  that has nothing to do with what it's actually testing — and that's confusing
  to debug from the outside. Case 2 below now says which sub-points are
  independent and which aren't; do the same for future multi-part cases.
- **A session's own launch flags can silently make a case untestable, with
  zero UI signal.** Ran an `Edit` during case 3b expecting the diff-review
  buffer to open; nothing opened. Spent real time checking `louiselm`'s
  remembered-permission store (exact-path match only, one unrelated rule on
  disk — not the cause) before finding it one layer out: this session's agent
  process was launched with `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions`, so the ACP
  `session/request_permission` call this whole feature depends on never fires.
  Confirmed session-specific by diffing against a sibling session from the
  same day with 17 normal permission requests. Lesson: for any case that
  depends on an approval/permission gate, state and verify the session's
  launch mode in Setup *before* running it — see the new note there.

## Cases

### 1. Live export of a real claude turn

Exercises `4e4a58b`: `Transcript:record` against payloads the real
`claude-agent-acp` sends, plus `record_user` for the prompt.

Fresh `:LouiselmChat` (claude). Note the session id (`:LouiselmSessionId`).
One prompt, chosen because it produces every block kind in one turn:

```
Do these three things in order, in this one turn. (1) Run the Bash tool on the absolute path: `wc -l /home/lotso/code/louiselm/lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua`. (2) Use the Task tool to launch one general-purpose subagent whose prompt is exactly: "List the top-level directories of /home/lotso/code/louiselm as one comma-separated line." (3) Write me a two-sentence summary of what you found.
```

When the turn ends: `:LouiselmToMarkdown`, leave the path blank, press Enter.

Expect: `louiselm: exported transcript to /home/lotso/code/louiselm/louiselm-<id>-<ts>.md`,
and in that file — a `## User` block holding **your prompt exactly as typed**, a
`## Tool:` block per tool call in the order they ran, each with the full
`rawInput`/`content`/`rawOutput` dump, and `## Assistant` blocks for the text.

Failure signature: a tool call missing entirely, tool blocks out of order,
the `## User` block absent or holding injected context markers rather than your
text, or a `## Tool:` block whose `content` is empty while the chat showed
output.

Prediction, already **checked offline and refuted** — do not spend attention on
it: I expected `merge_tool_call`'s per-field later-wins to silently drop earlier
`content` payloads. Across 7687 real multi-payload tool calls in your ACP logs,
and after replaying two real logs through the actual renderer, every earlier
payload turned out to be a placeholder, a streaming refinement, or a duplicate of
`rawInput` (e.g. a Task call's dropped `content` prompt is verbatim in
`rawInput.prompt`; a dropped diff hunk is verbatim in `rawInput.old_string`). No
unique information was lost. The live run just needs to confirm the shape, not
hunt for that.

**Result: PASS.** Evidence check (below) against the turn-1 prefix of the
jsonrpc log: 3/3 tool calls present, correct order, none missing, exactly one
`## User` block holding the prompt verbatim. Manually confirmed the `## Tool:`
blocks are in order (`wc -l` first, `Task` second with a nested `Bash` tool
call inside it via `parentToolUseId`) and the `## Assistant` block matches what
was actually said.

### 2. `:LouiselmToMarkdown` input paths

Exercises `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:266` — the real `vim.ui.input`, which
every test replaces with a stub.

With the case 1 session still open, run each and report what you see. **2.1
through 2.4 share the same open chat/session state** — if one leaves the UI odd
(stray notification, focus in the wrong place, anything that looks like the
crash below), say so before moving to the next one; don't assume a later
sub-point's result is clean.

1. `:LouiselmToMarkdown` then **Esc** at the prompt → expect nothing written and
   **no error notification** (cancel returns silently). Confirm no stray file:
   `ls -t ~/code/louiselm/louiselm-*.md | head -3`.
   **Result: PASS**, as reported.
2. `:LouiselmToMarkdown`, type `~/tmp/qa-export.md` → prediction: this **fails**
   with `could not write markdown file: ~/tmp/qa-export.md`, because
   `vim.fn.writefile` does not expand `~`. Confirm or refute; if it fails, note
   whether the message makes the cause obvious.
   **Result: prediction refuted, real bug found.** `vim.fn.writefile` doesn't
   return a failure code for a missing parent directory — it *throws* `E482`,
   which was never caught, so a raw Lua stack trace hit `:messages` instead of
   the clean notification. Filed and fixed as `louiselm-dim`
   (commit `6167df0`) — `writefile` is now wrapped in `pcall`.
   **Retest: PASS.** Clean `could not write markdown file: ...` notification,
   no stack trace.
3. `:LouiselmToMarkdown`, type `/tmp/nope/qa-export.md` (missing directory) →
   expect the same `could not write markdown file:` error, no crash, chat intact.
   **Result: same bug as 2.2**, same fix. **Retest: PASS**, same clean error.
4. `:LouiselmToMarkdown not-a-session-id` → expect `louiselm: session is not attached`.
   **Result: partially refuted, real (minor) bug found.** The error text was
   right, but it only appeared *after* being prompted for a path first — the
   not-attached check happens inside `to_markdown`, which the command only
   calls once the path prompt resolves. Filed as `louiselm-euj`, **not fixed
   this round** (small enough to batch with other UI-polish work later; not
   worth reloading the plugin twice in one round for).
   **Reconfirmed** while checking 2.5: still prompts for a path first, then
   shows `session is not attached`. Unchanged, as expected — nothing this
   round touched `louiselm-euj`.
5. After any of the above, where is the cursor? Expect focus back in the chat
   buffer, in the same mode you started in.
   **Result: PASS.** Checked by redoing 2.4 (the not-a-session-id case) and
   watching the cursor: it never moved, and mode was normal both before and
   after — same spot throughout. Focus was never stranded, even by the
   crash that used to happen here pre-`louiselm-dim`.

Failure signature: a silent no-op with no notification on a real error, a Lua
stack trace in `:messages`, or focus stranded in another window.

### 3. Export mid-stream, and during a permission decision

`Chat:to_markdown` is the **only** chat entry point that does not check
`self.decision_active` (compare `init.lua:1471`, `1648`, `1779`, `1800`, `1867`,
`1914` — all guarded — against `to_markdown` at `1543`, which checks only
`disposed`). That may be deliberate (writing a file harms nothing) or an
oversight; this case decides it.

**3a, mid-stream.** Start a long turn:

> Read /home/lotso/code/louiselm/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua and summarise each section in one line.

Export to **two distinct paths**, not the same one twice — `/tmp/qa-midstream-1.md`
while it is still streaming, `/tmp/qa-midstream-2.md` after the turn ends. (Originally
this case reused one path for both exports; that was a mistake — it makes the
superset comparison below impossible to check after the fact, since the second
write silently overwrites the first.)

Expect a normal success notification each time, a partial but well-formed first
file, the turn continuing undisturbed, and the second file a strict superset of
the first: every line the first file has, the second has too, unchanged, plus
whatever streamed in after — the transcript recorder only ever appends, nothing
is deleted or reordered retroactively.

**Result: PASS, superset confirmed.** First attempt reused `/tmp/qa-midstream.md`
for all three exports run during that turn, so only the last one survived to
inspect. Evidence check on that survivor (pinned to session
`21a0ede3-b65e-4f1c-935d-754f22126384`, log restricted to the prefix ending at
the last id the export also contains — see the cumulative-log ground rule):
**17/17 tool calls present, correct order, none missing**, all 4 user turns
present, file ends cleanly at the end of the assistant's response. No error
notification at any of the three exports, no crash, turn was never disrupted.
One perceptual "glitch" (buffer looked like a wall of text appearing at once),
traced to the final assistant message landing as a single large chunk (a
27-line bulleted list) — not a dropped update or corruption, nothing to file.

Rerun with two distinct paths (`/tmp/qa-midstream-1.md` mid-stream,
`/tmp/qa-midstream-2.md` after the turn ended) proved the superset relationship
directly rather than assuming it: `cmp` reports the two files byte-identical
for their entire common length (496172 bytes), with file1 cutting off
mid-word ("...pickers and" — the streaming chunk had only delivered that much
of "pickers and headers") and file2 continuing seamlessly from there through
the rest of the turn (986 → 1049 lines). Byte-for-byte prefix, not
coincidental length growth.

**3b, during a decision.** Requires a session **without**
`--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions` (see the Setup note above) — otherwise
no `session/request_permission` call is ever made and there is nothing to
open.

Reset the fixture and open a review buffer:

```bash
printf 'hello\n' > ~/code/louiselm/qa-diff-test.txt
```

> Use the Edit tool, not Bash, to change `hello` to `hello world` in /home/lotso/code/louiselm/qa-diff-test.txt

With the `louiselm-diff://` buffer open, run `:LouiselmToMarkdown` →
`/tmp/qa-decision.md`.

Expect: the input prompt opens on top of the review, the file is written, and
**after** answering the input you can still answer the review with `a`/`d`/`q`
and the turn completes normally.

Failure signature: the review closing or being answered without you (the failure
mode the guards on every other command exist to prevent), `a`/`d`/`q` going to
the input instead of the review, or the chat left with `decision_active` stuck so
`:LouiselmPermissions` keeps refusing afterwards.

**Result: PASS.** Run in session `aef3e4a2-4c64-4d24-80be-83cb9a48db4b`
(normal permission mode, confirmed via ground rules above). Review buffer
opened as expected; `:LouiselmToMarkdown` → `/tmp/qa-decision.md` succeeded
while the decision was still open — evidence: the exported markdown's tool
call block shows `status = "pending"` with the full diff (`old_string: "hello"`
→ `new_string: "hello world"`), proving the capture happened mid-decision, not
after. Log trace confirms the mechanism end to end: `session/request_permission`
fired (unlike the skip-permissions session), the tool call was `pending` at
export time, and transitioned to `completed` only after the review was
answered with `a`. `qa-diff-test.txt` read back as `hello world` afterward,
confirming the edit applied and the turn completed normally — no stuck
`decision_active`, no input/review cross-talk.

### 4. Resumed-session export vs the live export

Exercises the `user_chunk` path (`lifecycle.lua:186`) against the real agent's
`session/load` replay — the whole blog pipeline depends on it, because
`create-blog.sh` can only ever export what the agent replays.

Your logs confirm claude-agent-acp does replay `user_message_chunk`,
`agent_message_chunk`, `tool_call` and `tool_call_update` on load, so a resumed
export should not be empty. What is unknown is **fidelity**.

Restart nvim, `:LouiselmResume`, pick the case 1 session, and immediately
`:LouiselmToMarkdown` → `/tmp/qa-resumed.md` **without prompting anything first**.

Expect: the same tool calls, in the same order, and your case 1 prompt back as a
`## User` block.

Failure signature: header only and no blocks; tool calls missing while assistant
text is present; your prompt missing; blocks in a different order than case 1's
export.

Evidence: diff the two exports' structure (command in **Evidence check**). They
will not be byte-identical (`usage_update`, ids, timestamps), but the tool call
id sequence should match.

**Result: fidelity gap found, filed as `louiselm-d2o` (out-of-repo, not fixed
here).** By the time this ran, session `21a0ede3-...` had accumulated the
whole round's history, so the resumed export (`/tmp/qa-resumed.md`, 573KB, 66
tool calls, 18 user turns) is the full session replay, not just case 1's
turn — compared it against the original case-1-only export
(`louiselm-session-1-20260818-150448.md`, 3 tool calls, captured right after
that turn ended) as a prefix/subset check rather than exact-match. 2 of 3
case-1 tool calls present, correct relative order, case-1 `## User` block
verbatim. The missing one: a nested Bash call made *by* the Task subagent
(`parentToolUseId` set), present in the original live export with its full
command and output, absent from the resumed export entirely — the parent
Task call's own summary replayed fine, but its child call vanished. Confirmed
via the raw jsonrpc log that the agent process itself never re-emits that
event during replay (appears once, only during the original live turn) — not
a `louiselm` rendering bug, since `Transcript` only records what it's given.
See `louiselm-d2o` for full evidence, root-cause hypothesis, and why the test
suite couldn't have caught it (no fixture combines "replay" with "nested
subagent call"). **Not what case 4 predicted** (it predicted fidelity was
merely *unknown*, not a specific gap) — worth re-checking once case 5 runs,
since `create-blog.sh` uses the same replay path headlessly.

### 5. `create-blog.sh` against a real session id

Exercises `674939b`'s headless export path with the real agent and your real
`~/.config/nvim`, which the mock-agent tests cannot.

```bash
cd ~/code/louiselm
./blog/scripts/create-blog.sh qa-round claude/<acp-session-id-from-case-1>
```

Expect: `exported claude/<id> -> conversations/claude-<id>.md`, then
`created .../blog/post-qa-round`, exit status 0, and
`blog/post-qa-round/conversations/claude-<id>.md` holding the same content case 4
produced by hand.

Failure signature, in the order I think they are likely:

- `error: exporting ... failed:` with `timed out waiting for agent 'claude' to
load session ...` — the export gives up after 60s (`transcript_export.lua:25`)
  and a big session may legitimately take longer. Time it; if it is close to 60s,
  that constant is the finding, not your session.
- The written file is header-only (three metadata lines, no blocks) — the
  replay-fidelity failure from case 4, but through the headless path.
- Anything mentioning a _stale_ louiselm — the script prepends this checkout to
  `rtp`, but your config also loads the installed clone, so both copies are on
  `rtp` at once. If the error mentions a symbol that only exists in one of them,
  say so.

**Result: PASS.** `./blog/scripts/create-blog.sh qa-round claude/21a0ede3-...`
succeeded cleanly: `exported claude/21a0ede3-... -> conversations/claude-21a0ede3-....md`,
`created .../blog/post-qa-round`, no timeout, no stale-louiselm symbol errors.
`blog.md` scaffold matches the expected `{literalinclude} ... :lines: 1`
shape. As predicted when F3 was filed: the headless export reproduces the
same nested-tool-call gap (`louiselm-d2o`) — checked precisely for a genuine
`## Tool: ls -d ...` header (not a plain string match, since the transcript
by now also contains this bug's own filing text, which quotes the missing
toolCallId verbatim and would false-positive a naive grep); none found.
Confirms the gap lives in the shared `session/load` replay path itself, not
something specific to the interactive `:LouiselmResume` UI. Logged as a
comment on `louiselm-d2o` rather than a new finding — same bug, second
confirmation.

### 6. Does the highlighted fragment actually reach the published page

The end of the pipeline, and the part I most expect to be incomplete.

```bash
cd ~/code/louiselm/blog/post-qa-round
wc -l conversations/*.md          # pick a real range inside the file
$EDITOR blog.md                   # change `:lines: 1` to e.g. `:lines: 10-40`
cd ~/code/louiselm && ./blog/scripts/render-post.sh blog/post-qa-round
ls blog/post-qa-round             # expect *.nvim-transcript.html + nvim-transcript.css
cd blog && myst build --html --strict && cd ..
```

Then open `blog/_build/html/index.html` (or `myst start`) and **look at the
post**.

Prediction to confirm or refute: the highlighted fragment never reaches the page.
`render-post.sh` writes `<slug>.nvim-transcript.html` and `nvim-transcript.css`,
but nothing references either — `blog.md` still holds the plain
`{literalinclude}`, and `myst.yml` loads only `./blog.css` via
`site.options.style`. So I expect the page to show the excerpt as plain,
unhighlighted text, with no `<div class="nvim-transcript">` in the served HTML
and `nvim-transcript.css` absent from `_build`. If that is what you see, the
missing piece is the assembly step (swap the literalinclude for an include of the
fragment, and wire the generated CSS into the site) — that is a feature gap to
file, not a broken script.

Failure signature beyond that: `myst build --strict` failing (report the exact
warning it promoted), or `render-post.sh` erroring on the transcript's own
` ``` ` fences.

Also worth one glance: the exported transcript contains fenced code blocks and
`## ` headings of its own. Note whether an excerpt boundary lands mid-fence and
what that does to the rendered page.

**Result: prediction confirmed, filed as `louiselm-xrf`.** Used
`blog/post-qa-round` (scaffolded in case 5), `:lines: 10-40` (3033-line
source file). `render-post.sh` ran cleanly, `myst build --html --strict`
built all 3 pages with no errors. Evidence: `nvim-transcript.css` has zero
matches anywhere under `_build`; no `<link>` to it in the served page's
`<head>`; the only "nvim-transcript" string in the built output is the inert
`:class:` attribute on the plain literalinclude block, not the actual
generated `.nvim-transcript.html` fragment, which nothing ever reads —
`blog.md` still points at the raw conversation file. The rendered block does
show *some* syntax coloring (MyST's own generic `hljs`), which is why it
doesn't look broken to the eye — but it's not the nvim-generated
highlighting, and none of `nvim-transcript.css`'s rules apply to it. Priority
1: this isn't an edge case, the assembly step doesn't exist for any post.
Not fixed — real feature work, out of scope for a QA round. The
mid-fence-boundary question from the "also worth one glance" note wasn't
exercised: `:lines: 10-40` happened to land cleanly between a heading and
the next fence; noted as unverified in the bead.

### 7. GitLab CI — not runnable here

`.gitlab-ci.yml` only fires on the default branch when `blog/**` changes, and
`louiselm-8na` already records the ECONNREFUSED-under-bridge-networking risk with
repro steps. Nothing to run manually; whoever watches the first real pipeline run
closes that bead.

## Evidence check

Pin the log to the session under test first:

```bash
S=<acp-session-id>
L=$(grep -l "$S" ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/*claude-agent-acp*jsonrpc.log | tail -1)
```

```bash
python3 - "$L" <path-to-export.md> "$S" <<'EOF'
import json, re, sys
log_path, md_path, sid = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
ids = []
for line in open(log_path, errors='ignore'):
    try: d = json.loads(line)
    except Exception: continue
    if d.get('method') != 'session/update': continue
    p = d['params']
    if p.get('sessionId') != sid: continue
    u = p['update']
    if u.get('sessionUpdate') in ('tool_call', 'tool_call_update'):
        if u['toolCallId'] not in ids: ids.append(u['toolCallId'])
md = open(md_path).read()
md_ids, seen = [], set()
for t in re.findall(r'toolCallId = "([^"]+)"', md):
    if t not in seen: seen.add(t); md_ids.append(t)
print('log: %d tool calls' % len(ids))
print('export: %d tool calls' % len(md_ids))
print('in log but NOT exported:', [t for t in ids if t not in seen] or 'none')
print('order matches log:', [t for t in md_ids if t in ids] == ids)
print('user blocks:', len(re.findall(r'^## User$', md, re.M)))
EOF
```

Pass condition: `in log but NOT exported: none`, `order matches log: True`, and
at least one user block.

Validated against a known-good run before writing it here: I replayed
`20260610-132413-claude-agent-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log` through the real
`louiselm.session.transcript` renderer offline and this check reported 18/18 tool
calls with matching order.

What it cannot prove: that the _text_ of each block is complete, that your prompt
was captured verbatim (the log has no copy of it — you have to read the `## User`
block yourself), or anything about cases 2, 3 and 6, which are entirely
observational.

For case 4, compare the two exports:

```bash
diff <(grep -o 'toolCallId = "[^"]*"' ~/code/louiselm/louiselm-*.md | sed 's/.*= //') \
     <(grep -o 'toolCallId = "[^"]*"' /tmp/qa-resumed.md | sed 's/.*= //')
```

Empty diff = the resumed export saw the same tool calls in the same order.

For case 6:

```bash
grep -rl 'nvim-transcript' ~/code/louiselm/blog/_build/html/ | head
```

No hits = the fragment and its CSS never reached the built site, which is the
prediction.

## Cleanup when the round closes

```bash
rm -f ~/code/louiselm/louiselm-*.md ~/code/louiselm/qa-diff-test.txt
rm -f /tmp/qa-midstream.md /tmp/qa-midstream-1.md /tmp/qa-midstream-2.md /tmp/qa-decision.md /tmp/qa-resumed.md
rm -rf ~/code/louiselm/blog/post-qa-round ~/code/louiselm/blog/_build
```

Already in the tree before this round and unrelated to it:
`71c82ed5-9db8-44a3-9e64-e610a51b6cea.md` (a raw chat-buffer dump from the
permissions round — the lossy format this feature replaces) and
`qa-diff-test.txt`.

## Reporting back

Send me the session id, which case, what you saw, and anything surprising. I pull
the evidence myself. If something is wrong I will fix it, and you will need to
redo Setup before retesting.

## Findings this round

**F1 — `louiselm-dim`, fixed.** `Chat:to_markdown` (`init.lua:1561`) checked
`writefile(...) ~= 0` to detect a write failure, but Neovim's `writefile`
throws `E482` instead of returning nonzero when the destination's parent
directory doesn't exist — the check was dead code for that failure mode and a
raw Lua stack trace hit `:messages` instead of the intended
`could not write markdown file: ...` notification. Found in case 2.2/2.3.
Fixed by wrapping the call in `pcall` (commit `6167df0`), with a new
regression test in `tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua`. Full suite (235/235)
and `stylua --check` pass on the changed files. **Missed by the test suite
because** `tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua` covered the success path and
the "not attached"/"disposed" errors, but no case ever pointed `writefile` at
an actually-unwritable path.

**F2 — `louiselm-euj`, filed, not fixed this round.** `LouiselmToMarkdown
<bad-id>` (`command.lua:266`) always opens the path prompt before validating
the session id, so a bad id wastes a full path entry before the correct
`session is not attached` error shows. Found in case 2.4. Deliberately
deferred — small UX-ordering issue, not a crash, and batching it into this
round's fix would have meant reloading the plugin twice. Fix direction is in
the bead: a small `Chat:is_attached(session_id)` predicate so the command can
check before prompting. **Reconfirmed in retest** (case 2.4/2.5): still
reproduces exactly as described, unchanged.

**F3 — `louiselm-d2o`, filed, out-of-repo, not fixed.** `:LouiselmResume`'s
ACP `session/load` replay silently drops nested/child tool calls (ones with
`parentToolUseId` set — e.g. a tool call made by a Task subagent) while still
replaying the parent call's own summary text. Found in case 4, comparing the
original live case-1 export against a resumed export of the same session:
the nested `ls -d ... | paste -sd, -` call (made by the "List top-level
directories" Task subagent) is present in the live export, absent entirely
from the resumed one. Root cause is outside this repo — confirmed the
missing `tool_call` event never arrives from the agent process on replay
(raw jsonrpc log), so `louiselm`'s own `Transcript` code, which only records
events it receives, isn't at fault. **Missed by the test suite because**
no fixture combines a resumed-session replay with a nested/subagent tool
call — both paths are tested separately, never together. Practical impact:
`create-blog.sh` (case 5) uses this same replay path headlessly, so blog
posts built from resumed sessions may silently omit subagent-internal detail.

**F4 — `louiselm-xrf`, filed, not fixed.** The blog publishing pipeline's
highlighted-transcript feature is fully disconnected end to end:
`render-post.sh` correctly generates `<slug>.nvim-transcript.html` and
`nvim-transcript.css`, but `blog.md`'s `{literalinclude}` was never changed
to consume the generated fragment, and `myst.yml:11`'s
`site.options.style` was never made to include the generated CSS. Found in
case 6, confirmed by inspecting the actual built `_build/html` output rather
than trusting appearances — the page does show *some* highlighting (MyST's
own generic `hljs`), which would have looked plausible enough to wave
through without pulling the evidence. Priority 1: not an edge case, doesn't
work for any post. **Missed by the test suite because**
`test-render-post.sh` only tests `render-post.sh`'s own output in isolation
— no test in the suite runs a real `myst build` and inspects the served
HTML, which is exactly the gap this manual case exists to cover.

**Refuted before the round started:** the `merge_tool_call` later-wins
truncation I predicted from reading `transcript.lua:108`. Checked against 7687
real multi-payload tool calls and two full log replays through the real renderer;
every dropped payload was recoverable from `rawInput`. Recorded here so nobody
re-derives it.

title: blog/myst.yml + blog/blog.css: multi-post MyST site scaffold
description:
## Goal
A working MyST project under blog/, structured to hold multiple posts from the start, with a minimal starter stylesheet.

## Scope
- In scope: blog/myst.yml (MyST project/site config, article-theme base, discovers posts under blog/post-*/blog.md), a minimal blog/blog.css starter (just enough to prove the theme-attachment mechanism works — the real visual design is a separate, author-only task).
- Out of scope: the actual visual theme/branding (tracked in louiselm-0ee), any nvim-transcript-specific CSS (that ships alongside render-post.sh's output, not this scaffold).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `myst build --html` (or `myst start`) succeeds against the scaffold with zero or one placeholder post.
2. The project config is structured so adding a second blog/post-<name>/blog.md requires no myst.yml changes — multi-post support is real, not aspirational.
3. blog.css is attached and demonstrably affects the rendered page (not just present but unused).

## Testing
- Build smoke test: `myst build --html` exits 0 and produces output in the expected build directory — this is also what GitLab CI will run, so this test doubles as a CI dry-run.

## Notes
- This is the dependency root for the GitLab CI/Pages task — CI needs a buildable project to build.
- No dependency on the other tasks in this decomposition.
- Parent feature: louiselm-r1k.

title: Refuse louiselm command pickers while a permission decision is open
description:
After 0ed18d0 (louiselm-brx) the chat presents one permission decision at a time, but that queue only covers agent-initiated permission requests. The pickers louiselm opens for its own commands - file, skill, session resume, session switch, agent choice, remembered-permission management, session options - are still unqueued. Opening one while a permission picker is up makes an async provider such as the Snacks picker tear the permission picker down, its on_close fires with no item, and the request is answered cancelled without the user deciding.

Severity after 0ed18d0 is a lost prompt and a spuriously denied tool call, not a hang: the cancelled response releases the decision slot and the queue advances. That is why this is a task rather than a P0/P1 bug.

## Decision: refuse these pickers, do not queue them

Queuing every Picker.select behind the decision slot was considered and rejected:

1. Chained pickers would deadlock. Several flows open a picker from inside another picker callback: manage_permissions (rules -> revoke confirm), open_session_options (option -> value), and critically lua/louiselm/ui/diff/init.lua:114, where a review with several allow lifetimes opens a second picker WHILE holding the decision slot. That slot is only released when the second picker answers, so queuing it makes each wait on the other - the exact failure class louiselm-4wx and louiselm-brx removed.
2. Delayed popups steal input. A queued user-initiated picker opens at an arbitrary later moment, likely after the user moved on and started typing in the chat prompt, and the provider grabs input on open.
3. A leaked slot would freeze the whole UI instead of permissions only. Today a stuck decision still leaves the session picker and close_session reachable; behind one shared slot the escape hatches would be blocked too.
4. open_session_options auto-opens on state_changed -> ready and on attach (lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1070 and :1370), so with two sessions a config picker would surface long after the state change that caused it.

Refusing has none of those properties, is smaller, and cannot deadlock.

## Scope

- While a permission decision is presented (chat decision_active), user-initiated picker commands return false plus an actionable message, e.g. "answer the open louiselm permission request first".
- The auto-opened session options picker is skipped rather than reported.
- Exceptions that stay allowed on purpose: close_session, because it is the escape hatch when a decision is stuck and cancelling that permission is the right outcome when the session is being closed anyway; and cancel, which is not a picker.
- The diff review lifetime picker is untouched: it belongs to the open decision rather than competing with it.

## Acceptance

- Each guarded command returns its refusal without opening a picker while a decision is open, and works normally once the decision is answered.
- close_session still opens its confirmation while a decision is open.
- A diff review with several allow lifetimes still opens its lifetime picker.
close_reason: Implemented in b76a95d as specified: refuse, not queue. DECISION_OPEN_ERROR guards Chat:manage_permissions, switch_session, session_options, pick_file, pick_skill, resume_session, and the agent-choice path of new_session; open_session_options also returns early so the automatic picker is skipped rather than reported. close_session and cancel stay unguarded on purpose, and the diff review lifetime picker is untouched. Test: tests/ui/chat_spec.lua 'refuses command pickers while a permission decision is open' covers every guarded command, proves no extra picker opens, proves close_session still opens its confirmation, and proves the commands work again once the decision is answered. Full suite 197 cases, stylua --check, lua-language-server all clean. README documents the refusal and why it is not a queue.

title: Accept ACP nulls in session discovery
description:
## Problem

`:LouiselmResume` rejects valid ACP `session/list` responses when nullable fields are encoded as JSON `null`. Neovim decodes JSON `null` as `vim.NIL`, while discovery validation currently accepts only Lua `nil` or strings. A Codex response with `nextCursor: null` therefore reports `ACP session/list returned malformed data: nextCursor must be a string` and discards Codex sessions. The same mismatch affects nullable `SessionInfo.title` and `updatedAt`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `nextCursor: null` is treated as end-of-pagination.
2. `title: null` and `updatedAt: null` are accepted and exposed as absent optional values.
3. Non-null, non-string values for all three fields remain rejected.
4. A regression test exercises the JSON-null representation through session discovery.
5. Focused tests, full mini.test, StyLua, and lua-language-server checks pass.
close_reason: Accepted ACP JSON null for session/list nextCursor, title, and updatedAt by normalizing Neovim vim.NIL at discovery validation. Added regression coverage through the public discovery API. Focused session tests pass; full 126-case mini.test suite passes with writable XDG_STATE_HOME; stylua --check and lua-language-server checks pass.

title: Explain the LouiseLM vision and recursive identity
description:
## Problem Statement

The README documents development and implemented APIs but does not explain why LouiseLM exists, what the name means, or how its current ACP-backed Neovim foundation relates to the larger idea-to-software vision. Readers cannot yet understand the project before reaching the technical reference.

## Solution

Add a clear product narrative and an original hero banner at the start of the README. Present LouiseLM as alpha software whose north star is turning ideas into software, explain the attention-preserving workflow and its safety boundaries, and show the current manual workflow as one replaceable configuration. Preserve the existing technical reference beneath a concise bridge describing what works today.

## User Stories

1. As a new reader, I want to understand LouiseLM and its recursive name immediately, so that I can decide whether the project matters to me.
2. As a potential user, I want the vision separated clearly from current alpha capabilities, so that I am inspired without being misled.
3. As a creative developer, I want to see a strong default workflow presented as configurable, so that I can imagine building a different workflow with the same substrate.
4. As an operator, I want the vision to preserve my attention, ownership, and approval authority, so that automation remains empowering and legible.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The README uses LouiseLM as the project name and includes the exact recursive acronym: LouiseLM Organizes Unruled Intelligent Systems into Emancipated Language Meshes.
2. The opening states that LouiseLM turns ideas into software and clearly labels the project as alpha software.
3. The motivation explains that ideas arrive faster than sustained attention and uses the gardening example without clinical or medical positioning.
4. The vision covers interruption-free capture, later enrichment and explainable triage, focused deliberation, planning, dependency-shaped execution, agent implementation and review, human approval, and an observable operator control plane.
5. Neovim is presented as the deliberate home and cockpit, with headless automation and optional future capture surfaces rather than a promised editor-independent runtime.
6. Local-first ownership, configurable workflow boundaries, strong defaults, replaceable parts, and policy-controlled automation are explicit principles.
7. The current grill-me to plan to beads to coding-agent flow appears as one possible configuration; grill-me, beads, bv, bvr, particular models, and CodeCompanion are not presented as LouiseLM requirements. CodeCompanion is not mentioned.
8. Current ACP chat and session capabilities are distinguished from unimplemented idea capture, ranking, orchestration, and dashboard work.
9. An original banner depicts Louise Michel within a decentralized mesh of people, agents, models, skills, tools, voice capture, ideas, and code. It uses a red, black, and white Commune-era printmaking aesthetic fused with a modern systems diagram, informed by Metelkova street-art energy, with no labels or explanatory text.
10. Existing technical instructions remain accurate and mostly intact beneath the new narrative.

## Implementation Notes

- Expand the top of the existing README rather than replacing the technical reference.
- Add one project-local raster hero asset and reference it with a repository-relative path.
- Use project voice: one brief empowering manifesto-like passage followed by concrete language.
- The visual carries the Louise Michel reference; do not explain that reference in prose.
- Emancipation concerns ideas, workflows, and user choice, never unbounded agent authority.

## Testing Notes

- Documentation and image generation do not require an artificial red test.
- Inspect the final Markdown structure and rendered image reference.
- Run formatting, static-analysis, test, and diff checks required by the repository contract; report any unavailable gate.

## Out of Scope

- Implementing idea storage, capture devices, voice transcription, scheduling, triage, orchestration, dashboards, or agent review.
- Designing a formal plugin API, workflow event schema, storage architecture, mobile application, external daemon, graph UI, or swarm scheduler.
- Changing existing public Lua APIs or technical behavior.
close_reason: Expanded README with the agreed LouiseLM vision, recursive acronym, alpha/current-state boundary, configurable workflow example, attention and safety principles, and corrected single-file test command. Added and inspected an original 1774x887 red-black-white mesh hero as a 640 KB WebP. Verification: stylua --check passed; lua-language-server reported no problems; all 66 MiniTest cases passed after rerunning outside the read-only temp-file sandbox; git diff --check passed; external essay link returned HTTP 200.

title: Blog publishing pipeline never wires the highlighted transcript fragment into the built page
description:
`render-post.sh` generates a highlighted HTML fragment and a matching CSS
file for a transcript excerpt, but nothing in the publishing pipeline ever
references either — the built, served blog page shows the excerpt as plain
text (MyST's own generic `hljs` highlighting, not the nvim-generated one),
with no styling and no visual distinction from any other code block. This is
the last step of the blog publishing pipeline feature (`674939b`, tracked
under the now-closed `blog-publishing-pipeline` feature bead) and it does
not work at all — 0 of N published posts using this mechanism would ever
show the intended highlighted transcript.

## Observed

QA round for the transcript-export/blog-publishing features, case 6 ("does
the highlighted fragment actually reach the published page"),
2026-08-18, working from `blog/post-qa-round` (scaffolded by
`create-blog.sh` in case 5, session `21a0ede3-b65e-4f1c-935d-754f22126384`).

Steps run:
```
cd ~/code/louiselm/blog/post-qa-round
wc -l conversations/*.md   # 3033 lines
# edited blog.md: :lines: 1 -> :lines: 10-40
cd ~/code/louiselm && ./blog/scripts/render-post.sh blog/post-qa-round
# -> "render-post: wrote 1 fragment(s) and nvim-transcript.css to .../blog/post-qa-round"
ls blog/post-qa-round
# -> blog.md, conversations/, conversations-claude-21a0ede3-....L10-40.nvim-transcript.html, nvim-transcript.css
cd blog && myst build --html --strict   # built cleanly, 3 pages, no strict-mode errors
```

Evidence pulled directly from the built site:

- `find /home/lotso/code/louiselm/blog/_build -iname '*nvim-transcript*'` —
  **zero results**. The generated `nvim-transcript.css` never leaves
  `blog/post-qa-round/`; the myst build never copies or references it.
- `grep -o '<link[^>]*>' blog/_build/html/post-qa-round/blog/index.html | grep -i transcript` —
  **zero results**. No stylesheet link to it exists in the served page's
  `<head>` at all.
- The only occurrence of the string "nvim-transcript" anywhere in the built
  output is the inert JSON attribute `"class":"nvim-transcript"` on the
  plain `{literalinclude}` block — that's the `:class: nvim-transcript`
  directive on the literalinclude in `blog.md` being passed through as a CSS
  class with no matching stylesheet to give it any effect. The actual
  generated fragment file
  (`conversations-claude-21a0ede3-....L10-40.nvim-transcript.html`, produced
  by `render-post.sh`) is never included, referenced, or read by anything —
  `blog.md` still holds the plain `{literalinclude}` directive pointing at
  the raw conversation `.md` file, not the generated fragment.
- The code block that does render carries
  `class="block overflow-auto p-3 myst-code-body hljs"` — MyST's own
  generic highlight.js-based styling for an untagged code fence, applied
  because the literalinclude has no language hint. This is visually
  *something*, which is why the page doesn't look broken at a glance — but
  it is not the nvim-specific highlighting the feature is meant to produce,
  and none of `nvim-transcript.css`'s rules apply to it.
- `myst.yml` (`blog/myst.yml:11`) loads exactly one stylesheet:
  `site.options.style: ./blog.css`. No mechanism anywhere adds
  `nvim-transcript.css` to that list, conditionally or otherwise.

## Symptoms

- User sees: a published post's transcript excerpt rendered as a plain,
  unstyled code block — visually indistinguishable from any other fenced
  code block on the site, no indication a special highlighting feature was
  supposed to apply.
- System reports: nothing. `render-post.sh` reports success (and is telling
  the truth — it did produce a correct fragment and CSS file); `myst build
  --strict` succeeds with no warnings; there is no error anywhere in the
  pipeline. The gap is a missing wiring step, not a failure any current
  command surfaces.

## Root cause

`blog/scripts/render-post.sh` (writes `<slug>.nvim-transcript.html` +
`nvim-transcript.css` into the post directory) and `blog.md` / `myst.yml`
(control what MyST actually builds and styles) were built as two
disconnected halves. `blog.md`'s `{literalinclude}` directive was never
changed to consume the generated fragment instead of the raw conversation
file, and `myst.yml`'s `site.options.style` was never made to include
`nvim-transcript.css` (statically, or per-post if that file only exists for
posts using this feature). Exact files: `blog/scripts/render-post.sh`
(generation, confirmed working), `blog/post-qa-round/blog.md` (consumption,
missing), `blog/myst.yml:11` (styling, missing).

## Why it was not caught

`blog/scripts/test-render-post.sh` (referenced in QA_REVIEW.md as covered by
the existing suite) tests `render-post.sh`'s own output — CSS namespacing,
idempotency — in isolation. No test in the suite runs the full pipeline
through an actual `myst build` and inspects the served HTML, because that
requires the mystmd toolchain and a real build, which is exactly what this
manual QA case was written to cover that the suite structurally cannot
reach.

## Fix direction

Two independent pieces, both needed:
1. Have `render-post.sh` (or a follow-up step) rewrite `blog.md`'s
   `{literalinclude}` to point at the generated `.nvim-transcript.html`
   fragment instead of the raw conversation file — or have the fragment
   generation happen as part of a MyST-aware include mechanism rather than a
   side-channel file.
2. Wire `nvim-transcript.css` into the built site's stylesheet — either by
   adding it to `myst.yml`'s `site.options.style` (if it's safe to load
   globally) or by a per-post mechanism, since `style` currently only
   accepts `./blog.css` statically.

Options rejected: none evaluated yet — this bead is filed at the "confirmed
broken, here's exactly where" stage, not the "here's the patch" stage.

## Acceptance

- A post built with a `:lines:` range through the pipeline, when served,
  has a `<link>` (or equivalent) to `nvim-transcript.css` in its page head,
  and the excerpt's rendered HTML matches the generated
  `.nvim-transcript.html` fragment's content (real nvim `:TOhtml`-style
  highlighting), not the raw literalinclude passed through MyST's generic
  `hljs`.
- Regression test: build `blog/post-qa-round` (or an equivalent fixture)
  through `myst build --html --strict` and assert
  `_build/html/**/nvim-transcript.css` exists and is linked from the page
  that embeds the excerpt.

## Not covered

- Whether an excerpt range landing mid-fence (the transcript's own ` ``` `
  fences or `## ` headings) causes a *separate* rendering problem — the
  `:lines: 10-40` range used here happened to land cleanly between a
  heading and the next fence, so that specific risk wasn't exercised. Worth
  a follow-up case with a deliberately fence-straddling range.
- Whether the fix belongs in `render-post.sh`, a new orchestration script,
  or the `create-blog.sh` scaffold step — not decided here.
acceptance_criteria:
- A post built with a `% nvim-transcript: <source> :lines: N-M` marker comment, when run through `myst build --html`, has an `<iframe>` whose `src` is the absolute site-root path of the generated `<post-name>--<slug>.nvim-transcript.html` fragment, and that fragment file exists in the deployed `_build/html/` output, copied there via `project.static_files` in myst.yml (auto-maintained by render-post.mjs, not hand-edited).
- The deployed fragment's content is byte-identical to the one render-post.sh generated locally (proves the static_files copy step actually ran, not just that a stale/partial file exists).
- render-post.sh remains re-runnable: editing a `:lines:` range and re-running regenerates the fragment, blog.md's iframe block, and the myst.yml static_files entry idempotently, without destroying the marker comment that is the author's editable input.
- Regression test (blog/scripts/test-render-post.sh, part 3): a real `myst build --html --strict` against a fixture project asserts the fragment is copied into `_build/html` and that the deployed page's iframe references it at the correct absolute path -- this is the exact gap the bug's "Why it was not caught" section identified as structurally unreachable by the rest of the suite; it is now closed.

Superseded from the original criteria: no shared `nvim-transcript.css` file or `<link>` in the page head exists anymore. Investigation (see closing comment) found MyST's HTML build target does not pass raw HTML through from markdown at all (a literal `<style>`/`<pre>` in blog.md and the `{raw}` directive were both tried and confirmed broken), so delivery goes through an `<iframe>` loading a standalone per-excerpt HTML document instead -- which also makes CSS-selector namespacing and a shared stylesheet unnecessary, since the iframe already isolates each fragment's styling.
close_reason: Fixed: transcript fragments now wired into the deployed page via {iframe} + myst.yml static_files, verified by a real myst build --html --strict regression test (see comment for full design writeup).

comments.author: lotso
comments.text:
Fixed. Root cause confirmed and two more layers found beyond the original diagnosis:

1. Confirmed MyST's HTML build target has no raw-HTML passthrough at all: a
   literal <style>/<pre> in blog.md gets re-parsed and mangled (TOhtml's
   <span> markup silently stripped), and the {raw} directive only emits
   content for tex/typst export targets -- for html it prints the content as
   escaped literal text. Both empirically verified against myst v1.10.1.
2. `site.options.style` (myst.yml) only accepts a single string, not an
   array -- confirmed by a failed build ("style must be string").
3. The `{iframe}` directive, pointed at an absolute site-root path and paired
   with `project.static_files` in myst.yml, does deliver a fragment's exact
   bytes into the built page -- but `static_files` only accepts literal
   paths (no globs) and copyStaticFiles() flattens every declared file to
   one shared directory by basename, so two posts' same-named fragments
   would silently clobber each other without per-post-prefixed filenames.
4. `{iframe}` has no height option (only width/align/title/placeholder);
   the theme sizes the box via a fixed width-relative aspect ratio it does
   not expose. Fragment documents scroll instead of relying on a height we
   can't set.

Design landed on: standalone per-excerpt HTML documents (inline <style>,
no shared stylesheet, no CSS-selector namespacing -- the iframe's own
isolation makes both unnecessary), embedded via {iframe} at an absolute
`/<post-name>--<slug>.nvim-transcript.html` path, kept in sync with
myst.yml's static_files list by render-post.mjs on every run. blog.md's
authoring format moved from a `{literalinclude}...:class: nvim-transcript`
block to a `% nvim-transcript: <source> :lines: N-M` MyST comment (never
rendered), which render-post.mjs rewrites the following {iframe} block
against on every run without ever touching the comment itself -- this is
what keeps the pipeline re-runnable (create-blog.sh updated to match; both
its own and render-post's test suites updated, 38/38 passing, including a
new real `myst build --html --strict` end-to-end regression test that
verifies the exact wiring gap this bug reported).

Files: blog/scripts/render-post.mjs (rewritten), render-post.sh (header
doc), create-blog.sh (stub format), test-render-post.sh and
test-create-blog.sh (updated + new end-to-end case).

title: Rewrite AGENTS.md for strict idiomatic Neovim Lua
description:
## Goal
Replace the inherited Rust policy with a compact, strict, idiomatic Neovim Lua engineering contract focused on correctness, clarity, simplicity, and fast delivery.

## Scope
- In scope: rewrite the existing AGENTS.md in place for louiselm.nvim; target Neovim embedded LuaJIT/Lua 5.1; define StyLua, lua-language-server, and mini.test gates; lightweight red-green-refactor; LuaCATS/public API rules; module/state/table ownership; structured errors and UI boundaries; strict config validation; safe async vim.system usage; zero runtime dependencies; Neovim API preferences; dangerous Lua escape hatches; concise editing and completion discipline.
- Out of scope: adding formatter, language-server, test harness, Makefile, or CI files; implementing plugin code; including Beads/bv workflow documentation; generic standalone Lua 5.2-5.4 compatibility.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. AGENTS.md contains no Rust/Cargo/Clippy/unsafe-specific policy and no Beads workflow section.
2. The policy is concise and project-specific, with current-stable Neovim and embedded LuaJIT/Lua 5.1 as its runtime contract.
3. The document captures every agreed quality, architecture, error-handling, validation, async/process, dependency, testing, typing, and editing rule without speculative frameworks or compatibility shims.
4. TDD is mandatory for meaningful behavior changes but explicitly lightweight and delivery-oriented.
5. Formatting/static/test completion gates are explicit, and unavailable gates must be reported rather than claimed passing.

## Testing
- Review the rendered Markdown structure and run a text search proving Rust and Beads-specific instructions are gone.
- Check the diff for whitespace errors.
- No Lua project gates are runnable yet because this task intentionally adds no Lua/tooling files.

## Notes
- Rewrite the existing file only; do not proliferate files.
- Prefer enforceable rules over explanatory handbook material.
close_reason: Replaced the inherited Rust policy with a compact strict Neovim Lua contract. Verified no Rust or Beads terms remain; tracked and untracked whitespace checks produced no errors. Lua quality gates are not applicable yet because the repository has no Lua files, LuaLS config, or MiniTest harness.

title: Parse and validate Agent Skills metadata with lyaml
description:
## Goal

Replace LouiseLM's limited handwritten frontmatter parser with standards-compliant YAML parsing and a thin Agent Skills semantic validator.

## Scope

- In scope: load `lyaml` lazily whenever LouiseLM-managed local skill discovery is required; report a structured missing-dependency error and never install dependencies automatically.
- In scope: parse SKILL.md YAML frontmatter, validate required Agent Skills fields and known standard field types, and preserve the complete original SKILL.md for activation.
- In scope: recognize `disable-model-invocation` and `agents/openai.yaml policy.allow_implicit_invocation`; explicit-only wins on conflict and emits a warning.
- In scope: when optional invocation metadata is malformed or unreadable, retain a core-valid skill as picker-visible, mark it explicit-only, and warn.
- In scope: validate `allowed-tools` as metadata without granting or bypassing ACP permissions; warn when a SKILL.md exceeds 500 lines.
- In scope: ignore unknown extension fields without rejecting or warning, and remove the handwritten YAML subset parser.
- Out of scope: root precedence, symlink traversal, policy selection, catalog transport, and automatic dependency installation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. YAML features supported by LibYAML parse without adding LouiseLM-specific syntax.
2. Invalid YAML or invalid required Agent Skills metadata omits only that skill and yields an actionable diagnostic.
3. Core-valid skills survive broken optional invocation metadata as explicit-only picker entries.
4. Both known invocation controls are honored, conflicts warn, and explicit-only wins.
5. Missing `lyaml` is distinguishable from malformed skill metadata.
6. `allowed-tools` cannot change LouiseLM permission decisions.
7. MiniTest covers valid metadata, YAML syntax errors, semantic errors, extension metadata, conflicts, unknown fields, allowed-tools, and the line-count warning.

## Testing

Use fixture SKILL.md files and assert the public parser/validator result plus diagnostics. Do not test the handwritten parser after removal.

## Notes

`lyaml` is an intentional LibYAML dependency because LouiseLM should not own a partial YAML parser.
close_reason: Replaced handwritten frontmatter parsing with lazy lyaml loading and Agent Skills semantic validation; added explicit-only metadata diagnostics, dependency failure handling, documentation, and passing focused/full gates

title: Handle command and unknown permission requests in chat UI
description: Confirmed dogfood gap. The real claude-agent-acp file-edit probe emitted an ACP permission request and could be cancelled by a session event consumer. ui/chat/init.lua handles permission_requested only when operation.kind is file_edit; command and unknown requests are ignored, leaving the agent request unresolved in the interactive chat. Add a user-facing response path for every askable permission kind and cover a real fast-event-to-scheduled UI flow without auto-approving unscoped operations.
close_reason: Added scheduled command/unknown permission pickers, safe cancellation on dismissal and UI failure, disposal guards, tests, and documentation; all quality gates pass

title: GitLab CI: build and deploy blog/ to blog.bartab.fr via Pages
description:
## Goal
A GitLab CI pipeline in this repo that builds blog/ with MyST and deploys it to blog.bartab.fr via GitLab Pages, with zero Neovim dependency in the CI image.

## Scope
- In scope: .gitlab-ci.yml job(s) running `myst build --html` against blog/ and publishing the result as a GitLab Pages artifact; a note on the one-time manual DNS/CNAME step needed to point blog.bartab.fr at GitLab Pages (DNS itself is outside this repo's automation).
- Out of scope: rendering nvim-transcript excerpts in CI (explicitly not done — that only ever happens locally, output is committed); anything at the bartab.fr root domain.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Pushing to the relevant branch triggers a pipeline that runs `myst build --html` against blog/ and succeeds without installing or invoking Neovim.
2. The build output is published via GitLab Pages and reachable at blog.bartab.fr (once DNS is pointed, noted as a manual prerequisite).
3. The CI job fails loudly (not silently) if blog/ fails to build — e.g. a broken literalinclude reference.

## Testing
- Pipeline run validation: a green pipeline with a published Pages artifact is the acceptance test here, not a unit test.

## Notes
- Depends on the MyST scaffold task (needs a buildable blog/ project to point CI at).
- Benefits from render-post.sh existing for a realistic end-to-end validation (a post with real rendered excerpts) but does not strictly require it — CI can be stood up and proven against the bare scaffold first.
- Parent feature: louiselm-r1k.
